<p>After hearing Nerus’s guidance that she would come out of the gate as soon as she finished preparing, I stepped outside the gate and told Han Ji-hyeok everything that had happened in the room.</p><p>Of course, I hid all the details about my family and the Armband, instead explaining it vaguely as, “I don’t know the reason, but she says she wants to come out here and live with me.” After listening to my story, Han Ji-hyeok fell into deep thought, his expression serious for several minutes.</p><p>There was only one answer I wanted to hear.</p><p>I was waiting for him to say, “We really do need to subjugate that monster.”</p><p>‘Surely he’s not thinking of letting that monster loose in society, is he?’</p><p>“Chairman?”</p><p>Desperate, I urged Han Ji-hyeok for an answer. Finally, he made up his mind, patting my shoulder as he spoke.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon, the fate of the Republic of Korea rests on your shoulders.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>It seemed Han Ji-hyeok had decided to resolve the situation not by facing that monster himself, but by dumping it all on me.</p><p>‘Is that all?’</p><p>I knew that being was absurdly powerful, but seeing Han Ji-hyeok give up without even trying to fight filled me with doubt.</p><p>‘Maybe… he already fought it before I arrived?’</p><p>Then, a surge of disgust and disappointment welled up inside me—toward the chairman who had betrayed my desperation, and toward the Hunter Association itself.</p><p>“Ugh… fuck, this is insane…”</p><p>As I sighed deeply and muttered a curse in front of Han Ji-hyeok, every gaze in the room locked onto me. They stared with their mouths hanging open, as if looking at a madman.</p><p>But Han Ji-hyeok just nodded at the surrounding Association members, as if to say it was fine.</p><p>I had nowhere left to retreat. Whether I did this or that, I was screwed either way. Even after spitting out a curse from the bottom of my heart, my anger didn’t ease in the slightest—instead, my mind only grew more tangled.</p><p>‘Living with that monster…’</p><p>The Association members began offering various suggestions to Han Ji-hyeok, trying to control the situation somehow.</p><p>“First… we’ll secure a safe house for Echo and Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon.”</p><p>I agreed with that suggestion. There was no way I could take that monster home with me.</p><p>Han Ji-hyeok seemed to agree as well, and he tried to console me.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon, I don’t know if this will be any comfort, but don’t be too disheartened… The Association will do its best to protect you…”</p><p>It wasn’t comforting at all.</p><p>Soon, one of the Association members approached me with a thick stack of papers and handed them over.</p><p>“Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon, we desperately need information about Echo.”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>I stared blankly at the Association member, my expression clearly saying, *How the hell should I know?* The member coughed a couple times before continuing.</p><p>“These are the questions we’ve prepared. You need to ask Echo these and get the answers.”</p><p>“Haa….”</p><p>I barely managed to suppress the urge to smash the Hunter Association member’s head in with my fist for spouting nonsense while pretending to care about my safety.</p><p>“If you’re curious, why don’t you just ask them yourselves? Echo or His Majesty or whatever—they’ll be out here any second now….”</p><p>“T-That’s… How am I supposed to ask them?”</p><p>The association member stared at me like I was being ridiculous.</p><p>“No, wait—if even *I* can’t ask, how the hell am I supposed to make *you* do it? Have you ever even set foot inside a Gate? You people treat Hunters like disposable pawns you can just throw away on command….”</p><p>I’d already lost all self-control. Every thought that popped into my head spilled out of my mouth unfiltered. And then I said the one thing desk-job association members hated hearing the most.</p><p>“This is why non-Hunter association members get shit on all the time. Toss one of you into an E-rank Gate, and half a day later, you’d be a corpse. But here you are, sitting pretty at a desk with nothing but a mouth on you….”</p><p>The atmosphere froze instantly, and a heavy silence fell over the room. Unable to bear it any longer, Han Ji-hyeok stepped in, snatched the questionnaire from the association member’s hand, tossed it into the trash, and turned to me.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon, let me apologize for you… I know you’re not in the mood to hear this, but try to calm down. It’s embarrassing, but we’ve learned *nothing* from them over the past few months. Right now… you’re the closest thing we have to an expert on those beings….”</p><p>*Expert*? What was he even talking about?</p><p>“Do I *look* calm to you… huh?”</p><p>Then, every pair of eyes in the room snapped toward the Gate. The violet glow dimmed, shifting to black as an ominous energy radiated from it. With a *whoosh*, Echo and Nerus stepped out.</p><p>“It’s been a while. And yet, I see nothing but unfamiliar faces. Nerus, when was the last time I set foot in this world of lesser beings?”</p><p>“Yes, Your Majesty. By human measurements, it has been 1,672 years.”</p><p>“Has it? How things have changed. Though I suppose that’s only natural—humans tend to die the moment you look away. Wouldn’t you agree, Nerus?”</p><p>“Indeed, Your Majesty. Their short lives seem to drive rapid change.”</p><p>*A while?*</p><p>Echo spoke as if he’d visited Earth long ago. When I glanced at Han Ji-hyeok, his forehead was slick with sweat, a cold bead about to roll down his temple.</p><p>That careless remark from Echo’s mouth was going to send shockwaves through the world.</p><p>Because it meant the beings from the Gates had come to Earth *1,700 years ago*.</p><p>Echo turned to me, smiling as if genuinely pleased, and started toward me. I immediately lowered my head, ready to drop to one knee, but Echo waved a hand and said,</p><p>“I grant you the privilege of *bulbae*[1]. From now on, you need not bow or kneel each time you have an audience with me.”</p><p>“Your Majesty?!”</p><p>Nerus’s usual poker face vanished, replaced by an expression of sheer shock as he alternated his gaze between me and Echo.</p><p>‘Why the hell is he acting like that…?’</p><p>Maybe… not kneeling was some kind of enormous privilege…</p><p>“I refuse to accept a bow from someone carrying an old friend’s belongings. It would feel like bowing to the old friend himself, and that leaves a bad taste in my mouth.”</p><p>Rather than gratitude for the privilege, only one thought echoed in my mind.</p><p>‘Please, just shut up… Please, for the love of God, just keep your mouth shut…’</p><p>My anxiety spiked. After scanning my memories, there was no telling what kind of bombshell Echo might drop next.</p><p>Han Ji-hyeok bowed his head and spoke.</p><p>“Your Majesty, may I be so bold as to speak?”</p><p>“Permission granted.”</p><p>“We were thinking of preparing a place for Your Majesty to stay here. Would that be acceptable?”</p><p>“What are you talking about?”</p><p>Echo glared at Han Ji-hyeok with icy disdain. The Hunters around them couldn’t hide their alarm, and the non-Hunter Association members trembled in terror.</p><p>But Han Ji-hyeok showed no sign of intimidation. He met Echo’s gaze and said,</p><p>“Your Majesty, if there is anything displeasing, please command us.”</p><p>“I have decided to stay with this human, so it is only natural that I reside in his home.”</p><p>“Haaah…”</p><p>Before I knew it, a deep sigh escaped my lips. The people around me stared at me like I was a half-mad lunatic.</p><p>They weren’t wrong. I was already halfway there. Letting *that* monster into my house? That was insane.</p><p>“From now on, I will be with this human, and I forbid any surveillance. If anyone betrays my mercy…”</p><p>“There would be no excuse, Your Majesty.”</p><p>“Good. From now on, if you have anything to say to me, do so through Nerus. He will act as the intermediary between you and me.”</p><p>Nerus nodded.</p><p>I couldn’t even blame Han Ji-hyeok anymore. He had done everything he could for me.</p><p>He had risked his neck to say even a word to that monster, and now I was left with no choice but to accept my doomed fate.</p><p>“I wish to be alone with this human. Everyone, withdraw.”</p><p>“Yes, Your Majesty.”</p><p>Nerus and Han Ji-hyeok exchanged a few words before disappearing. An Association member approached me, pressed a set of car keys into my hand, gave me an encouraging nod, and then vanished as well.</p><p>“Now, guide me to your home.”</p><p>“Before we leave, there are a few things I need to make absolutely clear.”</p><p>“Speak.”</p><p>I had already made peace with death. Even if I died here, I planned to push through with my demands and take him home. It was better for me to die alone than to put my family in danger.</p><p>I took a deep breath and told Echo my conditions.</p><p>“First… you can’t walk around the human world looking like that.”</p><p>Of course, that appearance would have its demand in certain places, but it was forbidden in normal society.</p><p>“Hmm, is that so? Then how about this?”</p><p>Whoosh</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291039" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Surprisingly, Echo accepted my words without argument and changed his form. Black, ominous smoke enveloped him, and before my eyes, a phenomenon unfolded that could only be described as ‘magic’—his appearance transformed.</p><p>“I’m sorry to say, but that form is absolutely not acceptable either… We lowly creatures don’t have horns, so other humans would be shocked if they saw you like that.”</p><p>There was no way he could walk around society in that form.</p><p>“Is that so? Then how about this?”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291040" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Echo didn’t show the slightest annoyance at my demands. Instead, he seemed to find the whole situation amusing and started showing me various forms.</p><p>“No, that won’t work…”</p><p>"Then…"</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291041" loading="lazy">
</p><p>  "That one…"</p><p>***</p><p>After more than 30 minutes and dozens of rejections, we finally reached a conclusion.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291042" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Very well. Human, this is the form I took when I last visited this world. I cannot change further, so once you take me home, gift me with clothing.”</p><p>“Yes, that would be for the best.”</p><p>In the end, we decided it would be best to dress him in my family’s clothes, and I led Echo toward the car I had prepared in advance.</p><p>“Hoo… What is this thing?”</p><p>“This is called a car…”</p><p>It took another 30 minutes just to get in the car and start the engine. Whether he was genuinely curious or just pretending, Echo bombarded me with questions about everything. It was as if he truly had an interest in human society.</p><p>“This carriage is fascinating… Truly fascinating. The world has changed beyond belief since I was last here.”</p><p>I wanted to ask when, where, and why he had come before, but I swallowed all my questions. If I asked, I feared our connection would deepen, so I only answered his inquiries.</p><p>“Then, we’ll depart now.”</p>
